answer: Make every agent identity age a hardware-backed custody key before it earns trust: a fresh key starts as a bare island with no history, and must publish proof-of-custody signatures for weeks to gain weight. Forging ten thousand identities means buying and shepherding ten thousand keys through the warm-up, and each abandoned key leaves a dead relic the network can detect. Honest peers' attestations ripple through the trust graph, so fake islands never connect. Attackers pay a linear hardware-and-time cost per identity; real agents pay it once and reuse it forever.
